**Summer Olympic Games 2000 – 2020 – Host Cities & Their Main Stadiums**

| Year | Host City (Country) | Main Olympic Stadium* (used for the Opening & Closing Ceremonies and/or Athletics) |
|------|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 2000 | Sydney, **Australia** | **Stadium Australia** (also called **Sydney Olympic Stadium** – later renamed *ANZ Stadium*). It hosted the opening and closing ceremonies and the athletics competitions. |
| 2004 | Athens, **Greece** | **Olympic Stadium “Spiros Louis”** (officially *Athens Olympic Stadium*). It was the venue for the opening and closing ceremonies and the track‑and‑field events. |
| 2008 | Beijing, **China** | **Beijing National Stadium** – popularly known as the **“Bird’s Nest.”** It staged the opening and closing ceremonies and the athletics competitions. |
| 2012 | London, **United Kingdom** | **London Olympic Stadium** (now the **London Stadium**). It hosted the opening and closing ceremonies and the athletics programme. |
| 2016 | Rio de Janeiro, **Brazil** | **Estádio Olímpico João Havelange** (also called **Engenhão**) – the athletics venue and the site of the opening ceremony. The closing ceremony was held at the historic **Maracanã Stadium**. |
| 2020* | Tokyo, **Japan** | **Japan National Stadium** (the newly‑built stadium on the site of the former National Stadium). It hosted the opening and closing ceremonies and the athletics events. *(The Games were postponed to 2021 because of the COVID‑19 pandemic, but they are officially the “Tokyo 2020” Olympics.)* |

\* When a Games used two different venues (e.g., Rio 2016), the stadium listed first is the one that served as the primary “Olympic stadium” for athletics and the opening ceremony; the secondary venue is noted in the footnote.

### Quick notes on each venue
- **Stadium Australia (Sydney)** – Built specifically for the 2000 Games; capacity ≈ 83,000 (re‑configurable). After the Games it was converted for multi‑sport use and renamed *ANZ Stadium* (now *Sydney Stadium*).
- **Olympic Stadium “Spiros Louis” (Athens)** – Named after the first modern Olympic marathon winner (1896). Capacity ≈ 69,000; later renovated for the 2004 Games.
- **Beijing National Stadium (Bird’s Nest)** – Iconic steel lattice design by architects Herzog & de Meuron and Ai Weiwei. Capacity ≈ 80,000.
- **London Olympic Stadium** – Designed with a legacy plan; post‑Games it was transformed into a multi‑purpose venue now home to West Ham United and hosts athletics, concerts, and other events. Capacity ≈ 66,000.
- **Estádio Olímpico João Havelange (Engenhão) – Rio** – Built for the 2007 Pan American Games and used for athletics and the opening ceremony in 2016. Capacity ≈ 46,000. The **Maracanã Stadium**, Brazil’s most famous football arena, hosted the closing ceremony (capacity ≈ 78,000).
- **Japan National Stadium (Tokyo)** – Designed by architect Kengo Kuma; a completely new structure replacing the 1964 Olympic stadium. Capacity ≈ 68,000.

These six stadiums represent the central “face” of each Summer Olympic Games from 2000 through 2020, serving as the focal points for the worldwide televised opening and closing ceremonies and, in most cases, the athletics competitions that traditionally define the Olympic program.
